def to_space_key(space, default=None):
    """
    Map a patient-space label onto the corresponding ``SpaceKeys`` value.

    The label is matched case-insensitively and accepts the shorthand spellings
    (``"LPS"``/``"RAS"``) as well as the fully written out variants
    (``"left-posterior-superior"``/``"right-anterior-superior"``), optionally carrying a
    trailing time axis (``"LPST"``/``"left-posterior-superior-time"``) which leaves the
    patient axes unchanged.

    Args:
        space: the label to interpret, e.g. the ``space`` entry of an image header. ``None``
            means the label is missing.
        default: value returned when ``space`` is missing or does not name a space that can
            be expressed as one of ``SpaceKeys`` (e.g. ``"left-anterior-superior"`` or
            ``"scanner-xyz"``). Callers use it to define their own fallback convention
            instead of silently reinterpreting an unknown space.

    if not isinstance(space, str):
        return default
    label = space.strip().lower().replace("_", "-").replace(" ", "-")
    if label.endswith("-time"):  # e.g. "left-posterior-superior-time"
        label = label[: -len("-time")]
    elif label.endswith("t") and label[:-1] in _SPACE_LABELS:  # e.g. "LPST"
        label = label[:-1]
    return _SPACE_LABELS.get(label, default)

        Convert the affine from `LPS` to `RAS`. ``space`` is an optional NRRD field: when it is

            header[MetaKeys.ORIGINAL_AFFINE] = orientation_ras_lps(header[MetaKeys.ORIGINAL_AFFINE])
            header[MetaKeys.SPACE] = SpaceKeys.RAS
        return header

    def _declare_space(self, header: dict) -> dict:
        """
        State the patient space of the affine using MONAI's ``SpaceKeys`` vocabulary, so that
        consumers of the metadata do not have to fall back on a default convention of their own.
        ``space`` is optional in NRRD and `LPS` is the assumed space when it is not given, hence
        a header without ``space`` describes the very same geometry as one declaring `LPS`.
        A space that cannot be expressed as ``SpaceKeys`` is reported unchanged.
        """
        space = to_space_key(header.get(MetaKeys.SPACE))
        if space is not None:
            header[MetaKeys.SPACE] = space
        elif MetaKeys.SPACE not in header:
            header[MetaKeys.SPACE] = SpaceKeys.LPS
        return header

        self.affine_lps_to_ras = affine_lps_to_ras
        self.data_obj = None
        self.channel_dim = None

    def set_data_array(self, data_array, channel_dim=0, squeeze_end_dims=True, spatial_ndim=None):
        """
        Store ``data_array`` with its channel dimension (if any) moved to the last axis.

        Args:
            data_array: input data array.
            channel_dim: channel dimension of ``data_array``, ``None`` for a scalar volume.
            squeeze_end_dims: drop trailing singleton dimensions.
            spatial_ndim: number of leading axes that carry spatial (patient-space) information.
                Squeezing stops there, so that a spatial axis of extent one, e.g. a single slice
                of a 3-D study, is kept together with the geometry describing it.
        """
        arr = np.asarray(data_array)
        if channel_dim is not None and arr.ndim > 0 and channel_dim != arr.ndim - 1:
            arr = np.moveaxis(arr, channel_dim, -1)
        if squeeze_end_dims:
            min_ndim = 0 if spatial_ndim is None else int(spatial_ndim)
            while arr.ndim > min_ndim and arr.ndim > 0 and arr.shape[-1] == 1:
                arr = np.squeeze(arr, axis=-1)
        self.data_obj = np.asarray(arr, dtype=self.output_dtype)
        # a channel dimension that has been squeezed away no longer needs to be accounted for
        self.channel_dim = channel_dim if self.data_obj.ndim >= np.asarray(data_array).ndim else None

    def create_backend_obj(self, data_obj, channel_dim=None, affine=None, affine_lps_to_ras=False, dtype=None, kwargs=None):
        """
        Create an ITK image from ``data_obj`` and ``affine``.

        ``data_obj`` follows MONAI's convention, i.e. its axis ``i`` is the spatial axis described
        by column ``i`` of ``affine`` (channels last). ITK stores its buffer with the first spatial
        axis varying fastest, so the array is transposed into a C-contiguous ITK layout instead of
        relying on the memory order it happens to arrive with.
        """
        dtype = dtype or self.output_dtype
        arr = np.asarray(data_obj, dtype=dtype)
        is_vec = not is_no_channel(channel_dim)
        ndim = max(arr.ndim - (1 if is_vec else 0), 1)  # number of spatial axes
        if is_vec:
            arr = np.moveaxis(arr, -1, 0)  # ITK interleaves the components of a vector pixel
        arr = arr.T.astype(dtype, copy=True, order="C")
        ttype = (kwargs or {}).pop("ttype", None)
        img = itk.GetImageFromArray(arr, is_vector=is_vec, ttype=ttype)
        affine = np.asarray(affine if affine is not None else np.eye(ndim + 1), dtype=float)
        if affine_lps_to_ras:
            affine = orientation_ras_lps(affine)
        affine = to_affine_nd(ndim, affine)  # match the geometry to the spatial axes of the image
        spacing = affine_to_spacing(affine, r=ndim)
        direction = affine[:ndim, :ndim] @ np.diag(1 / spacing)
        img.SetSpacing(tuple(float(v) for v in spacing))
        img.SetOrigin(tuple(float(v) for v in affine[:ndim, -1]))
        img.SetDirection(itk.matrix_from_array(direction))
        return img

TOL = 1e-5


def rotation(ndim: int, seed: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """A right-handed rotation, so that studies are not axis aligned."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    q, _ = np.linalg.qr(rng.normal(size=(ndim, ndim)))
    if np.linalg.det(q) < 0:
        q[:, 0] *= -1
    return q


def write_study(path, data, spacing, origin, space=None, oblique_seed=None):
    """Write an NRRD study; `space directions` lists one patient vector per image axis."""
    ndim = data.ndim
    axes = np.eye(ndim) if oblique_seed is None else rotation(ndim, oblique_seed)
    directions = (axes * np.asarray(spacing, dtype=float)).T
    header = {"space directions": directions, "space origin": np.asarray(origin, dtype=float)}
    if space is None:
        header["space dimension"] = ndim  # `space` is optional in NRRD
    else:
        header["space"] = space
    nrrd.write(str(path), data, header=header)
    return directions, np.asarray(origin, dtype=float)


def geometry(image):
    return (
        tuple(itk.size(image)),
        np.asarray(image.GetSpacing(), dtype=float),
        np.asarray(image.GetOrigin(), dtype=float),
        np.asarray(image.GetDirection()).astype(float),
    )


def assert_same_image(actual, expected):
    a_size, a_spacing, a_origin, a_direction = geometry(actual)
    e_size, e_spacing, e_origin, e_direction = geometry(expected)
    assert a_size == e_size
    np.testing.assert_allclose(a_spacing, e_spacing, atol=TOL)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(a_origin, e_origin, atol=TOL)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(a_direction, e_direction, atol=TOL)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(itk.GetArrayFromImage(actual), itk.GetArrayFromImage(expected), atol=TOL)


def bridge(path, affine_lps_to_ras, index_order="F"):
    reader = NrrdReader(affine_lps_to_ras=affine_lps_to_ras, index_order=index_order)
    data, meta = reader.get_data(reader.read(path))
    tensor = MetaTensor(data, affine=meta[MetaKeys.AFFINE], meta=meta)
    return metatensor_to_itk_image(tensor, channel_dim=None), data, meta

def test_ras_tensor_is_converted_for_itk(tmp_path):
    """An `RAS` affine has to be flipped, an `LPS` affine must be left alone."""
    data = np.arange(24, dtype=np.float32).reshape(2, 3, 4)
    lps_affine = np.array([[1.2, 0.0, 0.0, 10.0], [0.0, 1.5, 0.0, -20.0], [0.0, 0.0, 2.5, 6.0], [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0]])
    ras_affine = np.diag([-1.0, -1.0, 1.0, 1.0]) @ lps_affine

    lps_image = metatensor_to_itk_image(MetaTensor(data, affine=lps_affine, meta={MetaKeys.SPACE: SpaceKeys.LPS}), channel_dim=None)
    ras_image = metatensor_to_itk_image(MetaTensor(data, affine=ras_affine, meta={MetaKeys.SPACE: SpaceKeys.RAS}), channel_dim=None)

    assert_same_image(ras_image, lps_image)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(np.asarray(lps_image.GetOrigin()), lps_affine[:3, 3], atol=TOL)
    for index in ((0, 0, 0), (1, 2, 3), (1, 0, 2)):
        physical = np.asarray(lps_image.TransformIndexToPhysicalPoint([int(i) for i in index]))
        np.testing.assert_allclose(physical, (lps_affine @ np.array([*index, 1.0]))[:3], atol=TOL)
        assert lps_image.GetPixel(list(index)) == data[index]

The repair is complete. Here's what was wrong and what I changed.

## Diagnosis

The reproduction compared two equivalent routes for the same study (reader → `MetaTensor` → ITK bridge) and reported affine gaps of 24/40/12 mm. Three distinct coordinate defects were involved:

1. **`metatensor_to_itk_image` ignored the tensor's `space` metadata** (the primary bug — the module still imported `orientation_ras_lps`, `MetaKeys` and `SpaceKeys` without using them). An ITK image is *always* defined in LPS, so a RAS affine — what `NrrdReader` returns by default — must be converted first. Without it, the image silently described a mirrored patient (hence gaps of exactly `2·|origin|` in the L/P components).

2. **`NrrdReader._get_affine` used the direction matrix untransposed.** NRRD's `space directions` lists one patient-space vector *per image axis* (rows), while an affine keeps them in its *columns*. Invisible for the supplied diagonal headers, but it skews every oblique study — exactly the "must generalize to new studies" trap.

3. **`ITKWriter.create_backend_obj` inferred the array-axis ↔ ITK-axis mapping from numpy memory layout.** The same tensor + affine produced different physical volumes depending on C- vs F-contiguity; the array is now transposed into ITK's layout explicitly.

Supporting fixes: the reader now declares its patient space with `SpaceKeys` (a header omitting the optional `space` field is reported as LPS, per NRRD, so implicit- and explicit-space studies yield *identical* metadata and never depend on a consumer's default convention); the affine is built from the header that describes the returned data ordering; the writer keeps spatial axes of extent one, conforms the affine to the image rank (`to_affine_nd`), and builds a vector image for channelled input. A shared `to_space_key` helper interprets label spellings (`"LPS"`, `"left-posterior-superior"`, case/`-time` variants) and leaves unsupported spaces untouched rather than reinterpreting them.

## Validation

- `python reproduce.py`: `consistency_check_passed: true`, `max_affine_gap: 0.0` (exact), with both explicit and implicit studies now reporting `LPS`.
- **Ground truth**: 60 comparisons against `itk.imread` (an independent implementation of the same NRRD contract) — 2-D and 3-D, axis-aligned *and* oblique, `space` declared as LPS/RAS/shorthand/absent, both reader flags — match in size, spacing, origin, direction **and** voxel values.
- A full physical round trip (reader → `MetaTensor` → ITK → file → reader) returns the same affine, space and data; index→patient points equal `affine @ index`.
- `tests/test_patient_space_round_trip.py` (62 cases) covers these invariants; I confirmed each of the four defects, re-injected individually, makes the suite fail (37/24/1/41 failures respectively).

Public API, reader metadata keys and `reproduce.py` are unchanged (the only API additions are an optional `spatial_ndim` kwarg and the `to_space_key` utility); nothing is keyed to the supplied arrays, affines or file names. I deliberately left `_convert_f_to_c_order`'s documented (if debatable) axis-reversal convention alone, as it is outside the reader→bridge contract under repair.
